title: break and continue: leaving a loop or skipping one turn

visuals.title: Match each statement with what it does

pairs.meaning: Ends the whole loop at once; the program continues after the loop
Skips the rest of this turn and starts the next turn of the loop
Leaves the switch only; the loop around it keeps going

pairs.term: break in the inner of two loops
pairs.meaning: Leaves only the inner loop; the outer loop goes on
Jumps to the update (i++), then tests the condition

visuals.title: One turn of a for loop: where break and continue land

stages.name: 1. Test the condition
stages.detail: If it is false the loop ends normally.

stages.name: 2. Start the body
stages.detail: The lines run from top to bottom.

stages.name: 3. continue? Jump to the update
stages.detail: The rest of the body is skipped. Go to step 5.

stages.name: 4. break? Jump out of the loop
stages.detail: The loop is over. The first line after the loop runs.

stages.name: 5. Update (i++)
stages.detail: Then back to step 1 for the next turn.

goal: After this you can use break to stop a loop early and continue to skip one turn, and predict what happens to the loop counter and the output.
warmup: You are searching a pile of 100 notebooks for your friend's one. When you find it you stop: you do not check the other 99. That is break. Now imagine you are marking exam papers and one paper has no name. You put it aside and take the next paper. You did not stop marking. That is continue.
definition: break ends the loop immediately. The program goes on with the first line after the loop. continue ends only the CURRENT turn (iteration). The program goes to the next turn. In a for loop the update part (i++) still runs before the next test. In a while loop there is no update, so you must change the variable yourself before continue. break also ends a case in a switch. These two statements are the 'exceptions' of a loop: they break its normal rhythm.
howItWorks: Study the flowchart of the first example. The loop test is a diamond. Inside the body there is a second diamond: i % 7 == 0. If it is true, the arrow does not return to the loop. It jumps out to the line after the loop. That is break. In the second example the arrow of the if goes back to the update of the loop. That is continue. The body below the continue is skipped for that turn only. Watch the trace of the second program: for i = 3, 6 and 9 the step shows line 8 (continue) and sum does not change. Three more things to remember. First, break and continue need an if around them. Without an if, the lines after them can never run. Second, in nested loops break leaves only the loop it is written in, so the outer loop continues (see the third example). Third, inside a switch inside a loop, break ends the switch, not the loop. To leave the loop from inside a switch, use a flag or return. A typical use: checking a prime number. When a divisor is found, break, because there is no need to test more numbers.

worked.problem: Print the numbers from 1 and stop at the first multiple of 7. Print Found: and the number, then Done.
pseudocode: IF i is a multiple of 7 THEN
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[i = 1]
  B --> C{i <= 20?}
  C -->|No| H[/Print Done/]
  C -->|Yes| D{i % 7 == 0?}
  D -->|Yes| E[/Print Found i/]
  E -->|break| H
  D -->|No| F[/Print i/]
  F --> G[i = i + 1]
  G --> C
  H --> I([End])

sample.title: break at the first multiple of 7

explanation.text: A normal loop that could run from 1 to 20.
Is i a multiple of 7? The remainder after dividing by 7 is 0.
Prints the number that stopped the loop. \n starts a new line first.
break ends the loop at once. The numbers 8 to 20 are never visited.
Reached only when i is not a multiple of 7. Prints the number and a space.
The first line after the loop. Runs after the loop ends normally or by break.

steps.note: Loop starts with i = 1. 1 % 7 is 1, not 0, so no break. Prints 1.
i = 7. 7 % 7 is 0, so the test is true. Prints the Found line.
break! The loop ends at once. i = 8 to 20 are never tried.
The computer continues with the first line AFTER the loop.

worked.problem: Print the numbers 1 to 10 but skip the multiples of 3. Also add up the numbers you print and show the total.
pseudocode: IF i is a multiple of 3 THEN CONTINUE
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[sum = 0, i = 1]
  B --> C{i <= 10?}
  C -->|No| H[/Print sum/]
  C -->|Yes| D{i % 3 == 0?}
  D -->|Yes| G[i = i + 1]
  D -->|No| E[/Print i/]
  E --> F[sum = sum + i]
  F --> G
  G --> C
  H --> I([End])

sample.title: continue skips multiples of 3

explanation.text: sum collects the numbers that are printed.
The loop would visit every i from 1 to 10.
continue skips lines 10 and 11 for this turn. The loop goes to i++ and tests the condition.
Printed only for numbers that were not skipped.
Added to sum only for numbers that were not skipped.

steps.note: i = 1. Not a multiple of 3, so print 1 and add it to sum.
i = 3. 3 % 3 is 0, so continue: skip printing and adding, go to the next i.
i = 6 is a multiple of 3. Skipped.
i = 9 is a multiple of 3. Skipped.
i = 10. Printed and added. Then i++ makes i = 11 and the loop ends.
Prints the sum of the numbers that were NOT skipped.

worked.problem: What does this program print? It has two loops. The inner loop uses break when j is 2. Write the output and explain which loop break leaves.
pseudocode: IF j == 2 THEN BREAK (inner loop only)
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[i = 1]
  B --> C{i <= 3?}
  C -->|No| K[/Print new line/]
  C -->|Yes| D[j = 1]
  D --> E{j <= 3?}
  E -->|No| I[/Print bar/]
  E -->|Yes| F{j == 2?}
  F -->|"Yes: break"| I
  F -->|No| G[/Print i,j/]
  G --> H[j = j + 1]
  H --> E
  I --> J[i = i + 1]
  J --> C
  K --> L([End])

sample.title: break inside nested loops

explanation.text: Inner loop: j = 1, 2, 3 on every turn of the outer loop.
break leaves only the inner loop. The outer loop continues.
Printed only when j is 1 (j = 3 is never reached).
Runs after the inner loop ends, once for each i.

steps.note: i = 1, j = 1. j is not 2, so print 1,1.
j = 2. break leaves only the INNER loop.
Back in the outer loop body. Prints a bar.
The outer loop goes on: i = 2. The inner loop starts again at j = 1. Prints 2,1.
The outer loop is finished. Prints a new line.

variations.when: Stop searching as soon as the answer is found
Skip unwanted values; the update i++ still runs
Change the counter BEFORE continue or the loop may never end
Stop the fall-through to the next case
Leaves only the loop it is written in

variations.way: Flag or function to leave all loops
variations.when: You need to stop outer loops too
variations.example: found = true; (checked by both loop conditions)

mistakes.wrong: if (x == 1) break;   // no loop or switch around it
mistakes.error: break statement not within loop or switch

mistakes.wrong: if (x == 1) continue;   // no loop around it
mistakes.error: continue statement not within a loop
No compiler error. When i is 2 the loop skips i++ forever, so it becomes an infinite loop.
No compiler error. break leaves only the inner loop, so the outer loop keeps running.

examTips: break = leave the loop completely. continue = skip the rest of this turn only.
In a for loop, continue still runs the update (i++). In a while loop it does not, so update first.
break inside nested loops stops only the innermost loop. Count how many times the outer loop still runs.
break and continue are usually inside an if. They have no effect on the lines before them.
Trace the loop variable value by value and mark the turns that are skipped.
romanSummary: break loop ko foran khatam kar deta hai aur control loop ke baad wali line par chala jata hai.
continue sirf current turn ka baqi hissa skip karta hai aur agli iteration shuru ho jati hai.
for loop mein continue ke baad i++ phir bhi chalta hai, lekin while loop mein khud counter badhana parta hai.
Nested loops mein break sirf andar wale (inner) loop ko rokta hai. break switch mein bhi use hota hai.

practice.prompt: What does break do inside a loop?
options: Ends the loop and continues after it
Restarts the loop from the beginning
practice.answer: Ends the loop and continues after it
practice.hint: Think of finding the notebook and stopping the search.
practice.explanation: break leaves the loop at once. The program continues with the first line after the loop.
1 and 2 are printed. At i = 3 break ends the loop before the cout.

practice.hint: Only the turn with i = 3 is skipped.
practice.explanation: continue skips only i = 3. The loop carries on with 4 and 5.

practice.hint: For every i the inner loop skips only j = 2.
practice.explanation: j = 2 is skipped each time. The output is i then j: 11, 13, 21, 23.

practice.hint: What happens to i when continue is executed?
practice.explanation: A while loop has no automatic update. When i is 2, continue skips i++, so i stays 2 forever. Add i++ before continue.

practice.prompt: Write a program that reads a whole number n and prints whether it is prime. Use a loop with break as soon as a divisor is found.
practice.hint: Try divisors from 2 while i * i <= n. A divisor means not prime.
practice.explanation: Assume prime, test divisors, and break at the first divisor, because more tests are useless.

practice.prompt: A switch is inside a for loop. A case ends with break. What does that break leave?
options: Both the switch and the loop
practice.hint: Which statement is the break closest to?
practice.explanation: break leaves the nearest enclosing switch or loop. Here the nearest is the switch, so the for loop continues.

quiz.prompt: Which statement skips only the current turn of a loop?
quiz.hint: It does not end the loop.
quiz.explanation: continue skips the rest of this turn. break ends the loop.

quiz.prompt: After break leaves a loop, which line runs next?
options: The first line after the loop
The first line of the loop body
quiz.answer: The first line after the loop
quiz.hint: Where does the arrow of break point in the flowchart?
quiz.explanation: The loop is finished, so the program goes on after it.

quiz.prompt: for (int i = 1; i <= 6; i++) { if (i % 2 == 0) continue; cout << i; }  prints:
quiz.explanation: continue skips 2, 4 and 6, so only 1, 3 and 5 are printed.

quiz.prompt: In two nested loops, break is written in the inner loop. What stops?
quiz.hint: break stops the loop it is written in.
quiz.explanation: The outer loop continues with its next turn.

quiz.prompt: In which loop is continue most dangerous if you forget to change the counter first?
quiz.hint: Which loop has no automatic update part?
quiz.explanation: A for loop runs i++ after continue. A while loop does not, so the counter may never change.
